text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Distribution of shareholders' certificates under mass selloff scheme is slow.
ADEVARUL

- The leu currency is expected to depreciate to 10,000 to 12,000 to the dollar in a year's time, Alexandru Ghiba, first vice-president of Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, says in a front-page interview.
- A government spokesman says the cabinet will analyse the 1997 state budget at the end of October.
- While the country's trade gap widens with every passing month, unpaid bills to Romanian exporters from foreign partners amount to $8.5 million, the newspaper says.
- Romania's central bank will sign an accord for a $175 million syndicated loan on Wednesday.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romania expects to complete its second nuclear reactor at the Cernavoda power plant by the year 2000.
AZI
- Romanian oil exploration company Petrom RA will drill well off Bulgaria in the Black Sea under a contract signed with Enterprise Oil.
LIBERTATEA
- Oil companies Shell and Agip have protested against the state monopoly in the distribution of fuel. Their protest comes one week after oil giant Amoco left the Romanian market, the newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The CEC savings back is ready to give loans at 15 percent subsidised interest for housing construction, but this will not solve housing shortages. Only 2,000 families will be able to get cheap credits and demand is much greater.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Two Romanian human rights defence organisations will oversee the November 3 elections.
- The opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc will have talks with leaders of other opposition parties to watch over the polls to guard against fraud.
- Oliviu Gherman, president of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), said that his party would not conclude alliances before the November 3 polls.
- Romania has 17,286,623 voters, said state secretary Adrian Duta, head of the government commission in charge of organising the elections.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The Central Electoral Bureau (BEC) will check the lists with signatures filed by retired general Nicolae Militaru, Romania's first post-communist defence minister, to back his presidential candidacy. He could be struck off the list of candidates if allegations of fraud is proven.

- All opposition parties in the November parliamentary elections should sign a pact to oversee the campaign and prevent fraud, says Ion Cristoiu in an editorial. Political alliances must wait until after the polls.

- The opposition CDR bloc's electoral goal to win a large majority to form a government and implement its programme, according to a CDR statement. The CDR will include in the cabinet other opposition parties which accept its programme.

- Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca says in an interview that the constitution does not bar him from running in the election. Tinca is a candidate of the ruling Party of Social Democracy for the upper house, the Senate, in central Transylvania.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Parties with reasonable and concrete campaign pledges will win the elections, says Ioan Gavra, campaign manager and vice-president of the National Unity Party (PUNR).
CRONICA ROMANA
- Anti-Semitic posters were pasted up around the headquarters of the opposition Social Democratic Union (USD) of reformist former Prime Minister Petre Roman, a leading presidential contender.
LIBERTATEA
- Beggars capable of working to be fined up to 200,000 lei ($61).
- Parliament has altered legislation to impose short jail terms instead of fines for certain minor offences. Each 10,000 lei ($3) of the fine to be converted to a single day in prison.
- Only one of 12 Romanians has a car. Tractors badly needed for agriculture are being exported as farmers cannot afford them.
- The newspaper publishes a report on 100 HIV-infected children who started the new school year.
ZIUA
- Ukraine's envoy to Bucharest said his country disagrees with Romania to join NATO before having signed the treaty between the two countries. ($=3,268 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
